body: Quick pass (UMA) @ 0754f88c: quick gate green on the final head (motion, app incl. golden_cl/project_roundtrip, ui), clippy clean, option-off byte-identical, verify on the real model pinned (a sunk path and a plunge through a lid are caught), body complete. Flagged ready; a feat, merges at the next cut. Not run: the finish3d heavy lane, the reporter's STEP part.

**Tested on the reporter's part from #1196 (4B52391).** The quick pass notes "the reporter's STEP part" was not run, so I checked out this head (`0754f88c`) and drove the real part through the motion API directly. The land model itself behaves as described; the choreography around the lids does not. **As-is I would call the option unusable on this class of part.**

**Setup.** The #1196 part (4B52391 STEP — a 171.45 × 19.05 wedge, V-crease at x≈96.5, two vertical stepped holes: Ø6.5 counterbores + Ø3.4 through-bores, centers at x≈28.6 and x≈142.9). `fill_openings(width = 12.7, tol = 0.01)` (the reporter's setting) then `parallel` with `stepover 0.6`, `clearance_z 30`, ball Ø6 and Ø10, tol 0.05.

**What works on the real part:**

- The bridge over each hole is flush. Lateral cut endpoints across the filled footprints sit within ±0.02 mm of the roof plane (row y = −12.45 across hole 1, x 25.4 → 31.8: −0.003 .. +0.023 mm).
- The lid holds under the tool — **no plunge ever lands inside a hole below the roof plane**. The dives down the walls are gone.
- The warning naming the openings is genuinely useful; it is how I found the third one below.

**What does not work: the path fragments around the lids.**

A cut line that should cross a filled hole as one continuous lateral bridge breaks into many short runs, and every break costs a full retract → rapid → plunge to clearance. The march sees non-cuttable ground intermittently over the lid — hairline gaps of 0.45–2.8 mm, one of them straddling the through-bore projection — and the skip phase flushes the line each time:

```text
Feed  (24.90,-12.45,7.09) -> (25.40,-12.45,7.08)
Feed  (25.40,-12.45,7.08) -> (25.40,-12.45,30.00)   retract
Rapid (25.40,-12.45,30.00) -> (25.85,-12.45,30.00)
Plunge (25.85,-12.45,30.00) -> (25.85,-12.45,7.05)
Feed  (25.85,-12.45,7.05) -> (26.46,-12.45,7.05)
Feed  (26.46,-12.45,7.05) -> (26.46,-12.45,30.00)   retract
Rapid (26.46,-12.45,30.00) -> (26.91,-12.45,30.00)
Plunge (26.91,-12.45,30.00) -> (26.91,-12.45,7.01)
Feed  (26.91,-12.45,7.01) -> (27.28,-12.45,7.00)
Feed  (27.28,-12.45,7.00) -> (27.28,-12.45,30.00)   retract
Rapid (27.28,-12.45,30.00) -> (30.09,-12.45,30.00)  2.8 mm air over the bore
Plunge (30.09,-12.45,30.00) -> (30.09,-12.45,6.89)
...repeating every 0.5-1 mm across the hole footprint...
```

Vertical feed moves (retracts + plunges), ball Ø6 stepover 0.6:

| | fill off | fill on |
|---|---|---|
| total in path | 58 | **294** |
| within 6.4 mm of a hole center | 22 | **166** |

Ball Ø10: 58 → 230. On the reporter's own settings this surfaces as their summary's "118 plunges @ 11.81 plunge feed" — and in the simulation it reads exactly as they described: the tool "picks up and goes over" each hole, over and over, crawling on the plunge feed. The reporter reports waterline works on this part; it's the parallel-family raster that shreds.

**Minor: the third "opening" is the crease, not a hole.** The reporter's warning says 3 closed openings narrower than 12.7 mm, but the part has 2 holes. The third is the roof's V-crease (x ≈ 88–102, full 19 mm width): a 2–3° fold. The closing treats the fold like a pit and lids it (lid z 4.46–4.78), which lifts the path 0.04–0.29 mm above the roof there — the only genuine above-surface lift in the path. Since lids only ever add, a shallow fold can't be lidded safely; a depth guard (skip depressions only a fraction deep under the closing plane) would skip this.

**Take.** The fill rule is right on the real part — it finds exactly the right openings, the lids are flush, the path never sinks, and the verifier still judges the real model. The problem is downstream: the drive surface fragments at the lid/rim boundary, so crossing a filled hole costs a plunge every ~0.6 mm instead of one lateral bridge. Worth digging into why the march's support query loses ground over the lids (my guess: the rim edges and step walls occlude the ball's tangent samples directly above the lid); the fill patch itself would not need to change for that. With that fixed (and a crease depth guard), this becomes what the reporter asked for.
Back to draft to apply the requested changes from the 2026-11-12T20:59Z review (Pencil/Corner/Flow with fill_openings, round-trip tests for the new file key, cheap notes).

Review fixes pushed (0754f88c..437f1535, plain push).

**Requested 1 - Pencil / Corner / Flow with the fill on**
- Pencil and Corner with `fill_openings` are now refused by name at generation, beside Geodesic: `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:846-858`, message `"{Pencil|Corner} cleans the creases inside openings, so it cannot fill them - clear 'Fill openings' or pick another pattern"`. The refusal happens before any fill or path, so no land note is ever attached to a crease path. Pinned by `operations::finish3d_fill_openings_refuses_pencil_and_corner_by_name` (both patterns are refused as `CommandError::Machining` naming the pattern, and the status stays `Never`).
- **Flow honours the lids, so it is not refused.** `multiaxis::flow3d` only reads the facets for the direction field (`build_field`, curvature claims that steer the line direction). Every column's height comes from `finishing3d::flow`, which grounds its seeds and march on `plunge_support` over `build_sups(drive)`. Parallel uses the same support, so the lids count. The flanks ride `rings_and_tail`, the waterline rings, which also honour the lids. Evidence: `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_land.rs:273` `flow_honours_the_lids_and_never_descends_into_a_lidded_pocket` uses an 8 mm blind pocket with width 10. With the fill off, flow reaches the pocket floor. With it on, no tip goes into the pocket below the top - 1 mm, and the deepest bite on the real plate is <= tol. (The 3.4 mm pocket fixture was too narrow for flow's lines to reach the floor even with the fill off, so it proved nothing. That is why this test uses a wider pocket.)
- The note can no longer claim a fill the path does not do. The only paths that carry it are the ones planned on the lidded drive.

**Requested 2 - round-trip of `ParamsDto::Finish3D.fill_openings`**
- `project_roundtrip::finish3d_fill_openings_round_trips_through_save_and_load` (`crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs:5392`): `Some(5.0)` loads, saves as `"fill_openings": 5.0`, reloads as `Some(5.0)`, and save-load-save is byte-identical.
- `project_roundtrip::finish3d_file_without_fill_openings_reads_none` (`:5410`): a finish3d file without the key reads `None` and saves without the key.

**Notes applied**
- Note 1: when nothing is filled, the path now says `land: no closed opening narrower than W mm found - the path follows the model` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/fill.rs:62`). Pinned by `finish3d_land::the_note_says_so_when_nothing_was_filled`.
- Note 2: the decision file's large-width line is reworded. A large width coarsens the grid and can miss a thin rim, which is safe because nothing gets lidded. An unbounded "all" would need a cell clamped by tolerance or tool radius.
- Note 6: UI hint (`mill3d_page.rs:262`) now reads "the walls stay uncut; the gouge check still uses the real model".
- The refusal decision (refuse vs. teach the crease walk to honour the lids, and the Flow finding) is recorded in `docs/decisions/1196-finish3d-land-fill.md`.
- Not done: notes 3, 4, 5 and 7 (watch items, nothing to change now). tbrasselle's findings on the real part (the raster fragmenting at the lid/rim boundary, and the crease being lidded) are not in this round. They are separate from the requested changes.

**Gate** on 437f1535: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (motion 141 s, app 605 s, ui 106 s, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. No snapshot PNGs changed, no labels touched.

Ready for a re-review.
